articles.headline: 5 dead, many trapped as Satya Niketan students’ PG collapses
articles.summary: A five-storey building housing students collapsed in Delhi's Satya Niketan area during a renovation. Five people were killed and five others were injured. Rescuers from the NDRF and local authorities pulled thirteen people from the rubble. The building was over 40 years old and reportedly had no sanctioned plan. Police have registered an FIR for culpable homicide.

articles.headline: Iran threatens harder reply after US attacks
articles.summary: Iran's top negotiator warned of a forceful response to any further US attacks on Iranian interests. This follows recent exchanges of fire between US forces and Iran-linked groups in the Middle East. Iran has maintained a stranglehold on the Strait of Hormuz while Washington continues to impose sanctions on Iranian entities to curb its economy.

articles.headline: UAE move may delay India’s bid to extradite Mahadev app kingpin
articles.summary: India's attempt to extradite Sourabh Chandrakar, the alleged mastermind of the ₹6,000-crore Mahadev gambling racket, faces delays. The UAE has sent an extradition request to Oman for Chandrakar after he was detained there on an Interpol red notice. Both the CBI and Enforcement Directorate are pursuing Chandrakar for massive money laundering and illegal betting operations.

articles.headline: 11 killed after drinking spurious liquor in MP
articles.summary: At least 11 people died and 25 were hospitalized after consuming suspected spurious liquor in the Baraj village of Madhya Pradesh. The incident occurred over the weekend, leading the district administration to order a magisterial inquiry. Police have seized several liquor bottles and arrested ten individuals in connection with the illegal supply.

articles.headline: Rising Ganga floods Patna
articles.summary: The Ganga and its tributaries have flooded several districts in Bihar, impacting approximately 2.24 million people. In Patna, the Punpun and Gandak rivers are flowing above the danger mark. Relief operations are underway with 20 SDRF and NDRF teams deployed. Rail traffic has been disrupted in some areas, and thousands have been moved to relief camps.

articles.headline: Between courts, Delhi paper leak cases caught in jurisdictional bind
articles.summary: Cases related to the NEET-UG 2024 paper leak and other examination frauds in Delhi are facing legal delays. A jurisdictional conflict exists between regular district courts and a newly designated special fast-track court. This has led to a situation where bail applications and trials for several accused are stuck in a 'legal limbo' due to a lack of clarity in court notifications.

articles.headline: HAL set to deliver first batch of trainer aircraft to IAF
articles.summary: Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL) is prepared to deliver the first batch of HTT-40 basic trainer aircraft to the Indian Air Force. This indigenous aircraft is intended to meet the growing training requirements of IAF pilots. The project, worth ₹6,838 crore for 70 planes, has faced previous delays but is now on track for serial production and induction.

articles.headline: Monsoon may end with July as its only bright spot
articles.summary: Data shows that July has been the only month with normal rainfall during the current monsoon season. June and August recorded significant deficits, and September has also started dry. Cumulative rainfall is currently at a 13% deficit compared to the Long Period Average. Nearly half of the country's major reservoirs are running significantly lower than their normal storage levels.

articles.headline: Infantino shrugs off calls to quit, seeks fourth FIFA term
articles.summary: FIFA President Gianni Infantino has announced he will stand for re-election in 2027, seeking a fourth term that would last until 2031. This comes despite criticism regarding several failed initiatives and calls from some football associations to step down. Infantino remains confident in his leadership and has ignored the growing opposition from European football bodies.

articles.headline: CM Shivakumar urges students to study abroad, be 'job creators'
articles.summary: Karnataka Deputy CM D.K. Shivakumar encouraged students to pursue higher education abroad and bring back knowledge to become 'job creators' in India. Speaking at a study abroad fair, he highlighted the state's efforts to provide scholarships and financial support. He emphasized that global exposure would help students compete at an international level and benefit the local economy.

articles.headline: ₹4L drugs seized from e-comm facilities: FDA
articles.summary: The Food and Safety Drug Administration (FDA) seized drugs and expired beverages worth over ₹4 lakh from various e-commerce storage facilities in Bengaluru. The raid targeted unlicensed storage and pest infestations at facilities linked to major online retailers. The department issued notices for failing to meet health and safety standards under the Food Safety and Standards Act.

articles.headline: TN identifies 2 potential sites for second airport
articles.summary: The Tamil Nadu government has identified two sites—Cheyyur and Manellore—for a potential second airport for Chennai. Both sites are approximately 100 km from the city. The Airports Authority of India (AAI) will conduct a feasibility study and submit a report. The project aims to decongest the existing airport and cater to the state's growing air traffic needs by 2030.

articles.headline: Rahul will lead India bloc, says Venugopal amid 'Vijay for PM'
articles.summary: AICC general secretary K.C. Venugopal stated that Rahul Gandhi will lead the INDIA bloc in the 2029 Lok Sabha elections. This clarification comes amid reports of alliance partners in Tamil Nadu projecting Chief Minister M.K. Stalin’s son, Udhayanidhi Stalin, as a prime ministerial candidate. Venugopal dismissed any confusion, affirming Gandhi's leadership role within the alliance.

articles.headline: Naga ancestral remains to come back from UK
articles.summary: The University of Oxford has agreed to repatriate 39 human remains and ancestral artifacts belonging to Naga tribes. These remains were taken during the British colonial era. The Naga Repatriation and Heritage Network (NRHN) will oversee the return process. This move is seen as a significant step toward restorative justice and honoring the cultural heritage of the Naga people.

articles.headline: SC orders SITs to probe into fraud motor accident claims
articles.summary: The Supreme Court has ordered the setting up of special investigation teams (SITs) in every state to investigate fraudulent motor accident claims. The court found that insurance companies were being defrauded by syndicates filing multiple claims for the same accident. The SITs will aim to identify and prosecute those involved in these scams to protect the insurance industry.

articles.headline: 4361 EMRS students clear NEET-UG 2026
articles.summary: A record 4,361 students from Eklavya Model Residential Schools (EMRS) have qualified for the NEET-UG 2026 medical entrance exam. This marks a 26.7% increase from the previous year. The Ministry of Tribal Affairs highlighted this as a success of the government’s efforts to provide quality coaching and resources to tribal students in remote areas of India.

articles.headline: Controlled aggression, the mantra for Priya in Asiad
articles.summary: Indian boxer Priya Ghanghas is preparing for the upcoming Asian Games with a focus on 'controlled aggression.' The Commonwealth Games medalist has been working with coaches to refine her fighting style, balancing her natural power with better defensive tactics. Priya is considered a top medal prospect for India in the 60kg lightweight category.

articles.headline: India's GDP Grows 8.4% In December Quarter, Surpassing Estimates
articles.summary: India's economy expanded by 8.4% in the October-December quarter of FY24, exceeding forecasts. This robust growth was primarily driven by strong performance in manufacturing and construction sectors. The Reserve Bank of India maintained its growth projection for the current fiscal year.

articles.headline: New Parliament Building Inauguration: Key Speeches and Significance
articles.summary: The new Parliament building was inaugurated with a ceremonial puja and speeches from leaders. Key figures emphasized the historical significance and the future of Indian democracy housed within the new structure. The event marked a new era for legislative proceedings in the country.

articles.headline: PM Modi Inaugurates Atal Setu, India's Longest Sea Bridge
articles.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the Atal Setu, India's longest sea bridge, in Mumbai. The 21.8 km bridge aims to significantly reduce travel time between Mumbai and Navi Mumbai, boosting connectivity and economic activity in the region.

articles.headline: RBI Keeps Repo Rate Unchanged; Economic Growth Outlook Positive
articles.summary: The Reserve Bank of India's Monetary Policy Committee decided to maintain the repo rate at 6.5%. The committee noted positive economic growth and stable inflation, suggesting a cautious but optimistic outlook for the Indian economy. Further policy actions will depend on evolving economic data.

articles.headline: Sebi Mandates Enhanced Disclosure Norms for Investment Advisors
articles.summary: The Securities and Exchange Board of India has introduced stricter disclosure requirements for investment advisors. The new norms aim to improve transparency and protect investors by ensuring they receive comprehensive information about risks and fees associated with investment products.

articles.headline: India's Services Sector PMI Rises to 61.2 in February
articles.summary: The Purchasing Managers' Index for India's services sector climbed to 61.2 in February, indicating robust expansion. This surge reflects increased new orders and business activity, signaling continued strength in the services industry.

articles.headline: Adani Group Announces Major Expansion Plans in Renewable Energy
articles.summary: The Adani Group plans to invest significantly in renewable energy projects, aiming to become a global leader in the sector. The expansion includes developing new solar and wind power capacities across India, aligning with the nation's clean energy goals.

articles.headline: Government Boosts Infrastructure Spending to Drive Economic Growth
articles.summary: The Indian government has announced an increase in capital expenditure for infrastructure development. The move is intended to stimulate economic growth, create jobs, and improve logistical efficiency across various sectors of the economy.

articles.headline: Manufacturing Sector Shows Strong Momentum in Recent PMI Data
articles.summary: India's manufacturing sector recorded strong growth in its latest Purchasing Managers' Index, reaching 59.1. This indicates a healthy expansion driven by rising production and new orders, reflecting industrial resilience.

articles.headline: Tech Startup Secures $50 Million Funding for AI Innovation
articles.summary: A leading Indian tech startup has successfully raised $50 million in its latest funding round. The capital will be used to accelerate research and development in artificial intelligence and expand its market reach globally.

articles.headline: India-US Trade Dialogue Focuses on Market Access and IP Protection
articles.summary: The latest India-US trade dialogue addressed critical issues including market access for goods and services, and intellectual property protection. Both nations aim to foster a more balanced and robust trade relationship.

articles.headline: New Policy to Promote Electric Vehicle Adoption Launched
articles.summary: The government has rolled out a new policy aimed at accelerating the adoption of electric vehicles. The policy includes incentives for buyers and manufacturers, alongside investments in charging infrastructure to support a greener transportation ecosystem.

articles.headline: Indian Agriculture Sector Faces Challenges Amid Climate Change
articles.summary: The Indian agriculture sector is grappling with the impacts of climate change, including erratic rainfall and extreme temperatures. Experts are calling for adaptive strategies and technological interventions to ensure food security and farmer livelihoods.

articles.headline: Supreme Court Issues Ruling on Corporate Insolvency Resolution
articles.summary: The Supreme Court delivered a significant ruling concerning corporate insolvency resolution processes. The judgment clarifies procedures and timelines, aiming to expedite the resolution of stressed assets and improve the efficiency of the insolvency framework.

articles.headline: New Education Policy Draft Focuses on Skill Development
articles.summary: A draft of the new National Education Policy emphasizes integrating skill development and vocational training into the curriculum. The policy aims to equip students with practical skills for the modern workforce and reduce the gap between education and employment.

articles.headline: India Joins Global Initiative for Sustainable Energy Transition
articles.summary: India has joined a new international initiative focused on accelerating the global transition to sustainable energy. The collaboration aims to share best practices and promote investments in clean energy technologies to combat climate change.

articles.headline: Healthcare Sector Expands Access to Telemedicine Services
articles.summary: The healthcare sector is witnessing an expansion of telemedicine services, improving access to medical consultations, especially in remote areas. This digital shift is enhancing healthcare delivery efficiency and patient convenience.

articles.headline: Indian Film Festival Showcases Diverse Regional Cinema
articles.summary: The annual Indian Film Festival concluded, highlighting a wide array of regional cinema. The festival celebrated cinematic diversity and provided a platform for filmmakers to showcase their work to a global audience.

articles.headline: Rising Inflation Concerns Prompt Central Bank Vigilance
articles.summary: Persistent inflation remains a key concern for policymakers. While economic growth is strong, rising price levels are prompting the central bank to closely monitor the situation and consider appropriate measures to maintain price stability.

articles.headline: International Solar Alliance Summit Focuses on Energy Security
articles.summary: The International Solar Alliance summit convened to discuss strategies for enhancing global energy security through solar power. Member nations explored collaborations on technology, financing, and policy frameworks to accelerate solar deployment.

articles.headline: India's Mars Mission Completes Key Phase; Data Analysis Underway
articles.summary: India's ongoing Mars mission has successfully completed a crucial operational phase. Scientists are currently analyzing the collected data to further understand the Martian atmosphere and geological composition.

articles.headline: Cricket Board Announces Squad for Upcoming T20 Series
articles.summary: The Indian cricket board has unveiled the squad for the upcoming T20 international series. The selection reflects a blend of experienced players and emerging talent, aiming for a strong performance in the series.

articles.headline: New Guidelines Issued for Handling Hazardous Waste
articles.summary: The Environment Ministry has released new guidelines for the management and handling of hazardous waste. The regulations aim to improve safety standards and reduce the environmental impact of industrial waste disposal.

articles.headline: Parliamentary Committee Reviews Performance of Public Sector Undertakings
articles.summary: A parliamentary committee is conducting a comprehensive review of the performance of various public sector undertakings. The review focuses on financial health, operational efficiency, and strategic direction of these government-owned entities.

articles.headline: India Participates in Global Cyber Security Summit
articles.summary: India participated in an international summit focused on enhancing global cyber security. Discussions centered on collaborative strategies to combat cyber threats and secure digital infrastructure worldwide.

articles.headline: Digital India Initiative Sees Continued Growth in User Adoption
articles.summary: The Digital India initiative continues to witness significant growth in user adoption across various digital services. This expansion highlights increased digital literacy and access to online platforms nationwide.

articles.headline: New Drug Approved for Treatment of Chronic Disease
articles.summary: A new drug has received regulatory approval for the treatment of a specific chronic disease. This development offers a new therapeutic option for patients and signifies progress in medical research.

articles.headline: Government Eases Norms for Foreign Direct Investment in Defense
articles.summary: The government has eased foreign direct investment norms in the defense sector to encourage domestic manufacturing. This move aims to boost technological advancements and self-reliance in the defense industry.

articles.headline: UNESCO Recognizes Indian Heritage Site for Preservation Efforts
articles.summary: A significant Indian heritage site has received recognition from UNESCO for its outstanding preservation efforts. This recognition highlights India's commitment to safeguarding its cultural and historical landmarks.

articles.headline: ADB Projects Strong Economic Growth for South Asia
articles.summary: The Asian Development Bank has projected strong economic growth for the South Asian region, with India expected to be a key driver. The report highlights recovery in domestic demand and improved investment climate.

articles.headline: India Eyes Greater Role in Global Supply Chain Diversification
articles.summary: India is actively seeking to play a larger role in global supply chain diversification efforts. The country aims to attract international manufacturing and become a key hub for global trade.

articles.headline: National Cadet Corps Expands Outreach Programs for Youth
articles.summary: The National Cadet Corps has launched expanded outreach programs to engage more youth across the country. These initiatives aim to foster discipline, patriotism, and leadership qualities among young citizens.

articles.headline: New Research Sheds Light on Renewable Energy Storage Solutions
articles.summary: Recent research has unveiled promising advancements in renewable energy storage solutions. The findings could significantly improve the efficiency and reliability of solar and wind power integration into the grid.

articles.headline: Parliament Passes Bill to Strengthen Consumer Protection Laws
articles.summary: Parliament has passed a new bill designed to strengthen consumer protection laws. The legislation aims to provide more robust safeguards for consumers against unfair trade practices and product defects.

articles.headline: India and EU Deepen Strategic Partnership on Climate Action
articles.summary: India and the European Union have agreed to deepen their strategic partnership on climate action. The collaboration will focus on joint projects for renewable energy, sustainable development, and climate resilience.

articles.headline: Startup Ecosystem Shows Resilience Amidst Global Economic Slowdown
articles.summary: India's startup ecosystem continues to demonstrate resilience, attracting significant investment despite global economic headwinds. The focus remains on innovation and sustainable business models.

articles.headline: New Guidelines for Air Quality Monitoring Released
articles.summary: The Central Pollution Control Board has issued new guidelines for air quality monitoring across urban areas. The updated framework aims to improve data accuracy and inform policy decisions for pollution control.

articles.headline: India Sets Ambitious Target for Space Exploration Missions
articles.summary: India's space agency has set ambitious targets for future space exploration missions, including manned missions and interplanetary voyages. The focus is on advancing India's capabilities in space science and technology.

articles.headline: RBI Tightens Norms for Non-Banking Financial Companies
articles.summary: The Reserve Bank of India has introduced tighter regulatory norms for non-banking financial companies (NBFCs). The measures aim to enhance financial stability and risk management within the NBFC sector.

articles.headline: Global Leaders Convene for Climate Change Summit in India
articles.summary: India hosted a global summit on climate change, bringing together world leaders and experts. Discussions focused on accelerating climate action, mobilizing finance, and implementing sustainable solutions.

articles.headline: New Scheme to Support MSMEs Launched by Government
articles.summary: The government has launched a new scheme to support Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs). The initiative aims to provide financial assistance, training, and market access to boost MSME growth.

articles.headline: Indian Railways Modernizes Fleet with New High-Speed Trains
articles.summary: Indian Railways is undertaking a significant modernization drive, introducing new high-speed trains. This upgrade aims to improve passenger experience and expand high-speed rail connectivity across the country.

articles.headline: WHO Recognizes India's Progress in Eradicating Diseases
articles.summary: The World Health Organization has acknowledged India's significant progress in eradicating several diseases. The WHO praised the country's public health initiatives and vaccination drives.

articles.headline: Cultural Exchange Program Between India and Japan Strengthened
articles.summary: A new cultural exchange program between India and Japan has been established to foster greater understanding and collaboration. The initiative will promote arts, education, and tourism between the two nations.

articles.headline: Parliament Discusses New National Security Strategy
articles.summary: A parliamentary debate centered on a new national security strategy aimed at addressing evolving geopolitical challenges. The strategy emphasizes modernizing defense capabilities and strengthening international partnerships.

articles.headline: India's E-commerce Sector Expected to Grow by 20% Annually
articles.summary: The Indian e-commerce sector is projected to grow at a rate of 20% annually over the next five years. This growth is driven by increasing internet penetration and changing consumer preferences.

articles.headline: New Regulations for Data Privacy Introduced
articles.summary: The government has introduced new regulations for data privacy, aimed at protecting citizens' personal information. The rules govern the collection, processing, and storage of data by organizations.

articles.headline: India Strengthens Ties with African Nations in Trade and Investment
articles.summary: India is enhancing its strategic partnership with African nations, focusing on trade and investment. Discussions aim to boost economic cooperation and explore new avenues for mutual growth.

articles.headline: Government Boosts Funding for Scientific Research and Development
articles.summary: The government has increased funding for scientific research and development initiatives. This investment aims to foster innovation and address key national challenges through scientific advancement.

articles.headline: India to Push for Stronger Ties in AI, Deep Tech & Semicon at BRICS Meet
articles.summary: India will advocate for closer research collaboration and government-to-government partnerships in AI, advanced computing, quantum technologies, and semiconductors at the upcoming BRICS summit. The focus is on countering AI monopolies and de-risking supply chains.

articles.headline: Record `1.55 Lakh Crore Online Sales Expected This Festive Season
articles.summary: Online sales are projected to reach a record Rs 1.50-1.55 lakh crore this festive season, an increase of 25-29% year-on-year. Quick commerce is expected to capture 16% of this GMV, driven by increasing consumer demand.

articles.headline: Foreign Tourist Arrivals Seen Flat This Year
articles.summary: Foreign tourist arrivals in India are expected to remain flat this year compared to last year. Industry bodies cite a lack of marketing activities and geopolitical issues driving up travel costs as major concerns.

articles.headline: Tech Synergy for Cementing BRICS
articles.summary: India aims to strengthen cooperation in AI, deep tech, and semiconductors at the BRICS meet. Focus areas include countering AI monopolies, sharing compute infrastructure, and exporting its digital public infrastructure stack.

articles.headline: ICAI Mulls PE Investment in Non-audit Biz for Better Solvency Ratios
articles.summary: The ICAI is considering allowing PE investment in non-assurance services of accounting firms, with assurance practices ring-fenced. This aims to boost the firms' growth and potentially improve their solvency ratios.

articles.headline: Content Creators Chart New Path to Monetisation
articles.summary: Tightening margins are pushing content creators toward YouTube for IP ownership and monetization. YouTube is becoming a key platform for premium, long-form content, with companies like Balaji Telefilms launching YouTube-led offerings.

articles.headline: New Chief to Address Operational Gaps at Air India
articles.summary: Tewolde Gebremariam takes charge at Air India, tasked with improving safety, operational reliability, and stemming losses. He faces the challenge of piloting the airline through a high-pressure environment.

articles.headline: Largest Spacetech Funding in India: Pixxel Bags $100 million
articles.summary: Satellite imaging startup Pixxel raised $100 million, the largest funding round in India's spacetech sector. The funds will support satellite manufacturing and constellation business expansion.

articles.headline: More Threats from Pakistan Provinces Than Neighbours' Border
articles.summary: Punjab CM Maryam Nawaz stated her province faces greater security threats from its own provinces than from neighboring countries, highlighting internal security concerns.

articles.headline: Manipur Voter Rolls: Women Continue to Outnumber Men
articles.summary: In Manipur's final electoral rolls, women voters continue to outnumber men, with a gender ratio of 1,056, significantly higher than the national average. The total number of registered voters is 19,60,620.

articles.headline: 5 Students Dead, Many Trapped in Delhi Building Collapse
articles.summary: A five-storey building collapsed in Delhi, killing five students and trapping many. Repair work was underway in the basement at the time of the collapse, which also damaged several vehicles.

articles.headline: AAP on Back Foot in Punjab as Govt Employees Escalate Stir
articles.summary: The AAP government in Punjab faces an intensifying challenge from its own employees ahead of assembly polls. Agitations over pending DA arrears and other demands are gathering momentum, with planned protests against ministers.

articles.headline: CM ED Moves to Seek Cayman Data in TMC Fund Probe
articles.summary: The ED is seeking Cayman Islands data via a letter rogatory to investigate alleged diversion of TMC funds to an aviation entity. The probe aims to identify beneficial owners and the source of funds, with TMC denying allegations.

articles.headline: KC-390 Can Meet India’s Transport Needs, Says Embraer
articles.summary: Embraer is confident its KC-390 Millennium aircraft meets India's requirements for 60 medium transport aircraft. It offers advanced capabilities and cost-effectiveness, with potential for local manufacturing.

articles.headline: 6 Cops in a Soup Over Birthday Cake Video
articles.summary: Six policemen in Maharajganj, UP, were suspended for alleged indiscipline and negligence after a video surfaced showing them celebrating a birthday inside a police outpost.

articles.headline: 135 Films, 40 Countries: J&K Hosts First Int’l Film Festival From Today
articles.summary: The J&K government is hosting its first international film festival in Srinagar, featuring 135 films from 40 countries. Prominent Bollywood personalities are expected to attend the four-day event.

articles.headline: Textile Exports Show 4.5% Growth to Rs 3.25 Lakh Crore
articles.summary: India's textile and apparel exports, including handicrafts, are projected to grow at a CAGR of 4.5% between 2019-20 and 2025-26, reaching Rs 3.25 lakh crore. FTAs are expected to boost competitiveness.

articles.headline: RBI’s Liquidity Test may Set Future Course
articles.summary: The RBI's 30-day VRRR auction outcome will guide its management of record Rs 10.5 lakh crore liquidity from FCNR(B) scheme. Additional tools like dollar swaps and OMOs may be deployed.

articles.headline: India Chases IPO Gold, Demat Additions Hit a 7-Month High
articles.summary: New demat account additions rose to a seven-month high in August, reaching 3.27 million. Robust IPO activity and a recovery in small and mid-caps have drawn more retail investors.

articles.headline: Fresh Offer Flow to Help Cos Raise Over 7,000 crore This Week
articles.summary: The primary market is set for a busy week with 16 companies planning to raise over Rs 7,190 crore through IPOs. This activity is driven by strong investor sentiment and a robust IPO pipeline.

articles.headline: SC to Hear Plea on Unpredictable Airfare Fluctuations
articles.summary: The Supreme Court will hear a plea seeking regulatory guidelines to control unpredictable fluctuations in airfare and ancillary charges imposed by private airlines. The Centre has fast-tracked framing of new aviation rules.

articles.headline: Haier India Revenue Crosses $1 b Despite Sluggish Market
articles.summary: Haier Appliances India crossed the $1-billion revenue mark, showing robust growth despite a sluggish market. The company aims to expand its product portfolio, manufacturing, and service infrastructure.

articles.headline: HUL’s Next Growth Cycle: MD Changes User Habits
articles.summary: HUL's MD identifies changing consumer habits, driven by factors like LPG adoption and tap water access, as key to its next growth cycle. The company is transforming its portfolio towards higher-growth areas.

articles.headline: B2B Firms Using Fresh Capital to Repay and Restructure Debt
articles.summary: Indian B2B companies like Zetwerk and Infra.Market are using fresh capital to repay debt and restructure finances. This trend reflects the need to manage accumulated debt from high-growth phases.

articles.headline: Foreign University Influx Fuels Indian Edtech Resurgence
articles.summary: The entry of foreign universities is boosting demand for online higher education and professional courses in India, benefiting edtech firms like Simplilearn and Scaler. UGC has issued LoIs to 15 foreign institutions.

articles.headline: Data Centre Capacity to Triple to 6 GW by 2029
articles.summary: India's data centre capacity is set to triple from 1.6 GW to 6 GW by 2029, with significant investments announced across states, particularly Telangana. AI surge is a key driver for this expansion.

articles.headline: Sustainability Anchors Growth, ITC CMD Urges Balance
articles.summary: ITC CMD Sanjiv Puri advocates for integrating sustainability and inclusive growth into corporate business models, emphasizing that economic progress cannot be isolated from sustainability. He calls for responsible competitiveness.

articles.headline: Goyal Urges Innovators to Build Social Solutions
articles.summary: Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal called on innovators to develop low-cost, sustainable solutions for social impact, highlighting the potential for profitable ventures that serve society.

articles.headline: Technology Seen as Responsible Growth Driver
articles.summary: Panelists at the Social Impact Summit discussed technology's role in mitigating the education divide and empowering communities. They stressed that technology should augment, not replace, human interaction.

articles.headline: Inclusion Must Mean Real Ownership
articles.summary: Panelists at the Social Impact Summit stressed the need for genuine inclusion, with young people demanding active participation in decision-making. Broadening the definition of inclusion is crucial for meaningful change.

articles.headline: Recycled Gold Powers Community-Led Disaster Strategies
articles.summary: Recycled gold is playing a role in the circular economy, saving foreign exchange. The discussion highlighted a shift towards disaster mitigation and resilience, with technology aiding community-led initiatives.

articles.headline: US Envoys Make First Kyiv Visit Amid Ukraine War Peace Push
articles.summary: US peace envoys met Ukrainian President Zelenskyy in Kyiv, renewing efforts to end the Russia-Ukraine war. Zelenskyy stated Ukraine has peace proposals ready and seeks firm security guarantees.

articles.headline: OPEC+ Keeps Output Targets Unchanged Amid Iran War
articles.summary: OPEC+ nations will maintain oil production targets unchanged in October, despite the Iran conflict disrupting supply. This aligns with their roadmap to hold targets steady through year-end.

articles.headline: Netanyahu Orders West Bank Settler Outposts Cleared
articles.summary: Israeli PM Netanyahu ordered unauthorized settler outposts in the West Bank to be dismantled amid US pressure. This follows increasing settler attacks against Palestinians.

articles.headline: Kimi Antonelli Wins Monza GP from Back of Grid
articles.summary: Kimi Antonelli won the Italian Grand Prix from 19th position, becoming the first Italian to win his home race in 60 years. The victory marks a significant achievement for the young driver.

articles.headline: Barca Fire 5 Past Valencia
articles.summary: Barcelona secured a commanding 5-0 victory over Valencia, maintaining their 100% start to the new LaLiga season. Fermin Lopez scored a goal and created two others in the dominant performance.

articles.headline: Arsenal Win, Man United Held
articles.summary: Arsenal rallied to a 2-1 win against Chelsea, maintaining their perfect start to the Premier League. Manchester United drew 2-2 with Everton, twice leading but failing to secure a victory.

articles.headline: Sabalenka Keeps 3-peat Hopes Alive with Win
articles.summary: World number one Aryna Sabalenka reached the US Open quarter-finals, defeating Taylor Townsend. She needs to win in New York to retain her No 1 ranking.

articles.headline: ICAI Explores PE Funding for Consultancy, Accounting
articles.summary: The ICAI is examining the possibility of allowing private equity investment in non-assurance services of accounting firms, with a clear split between assurance and non-assurance practices.

articles.headline: Finmin Secures $1 Billion IFC Funding for MSMEs
articles.summary: India has secured $1 billion in funding from the IFC to provide long-term credit to MSMEs through banks and financial institutions. This facility aims to address a key gap in the sector.

articles.headline: US Inflation Data, Crude Oil to Steer Bullion This Week
articles.summary: Upcoming US inflation figures, crude oil price movements, and geopolitical tensions in West Asia will be key triggers for gold and silver prices this week, analysts predict.

articles.headline: Turkey Lifts Year-end Inflation Forecast to 28.4%
articles.summary: Turkey has raised its year-end inflation forecast to 28.4%, with the West Asia war cited as a significant factor. The government expects inflation to start declining in Q4 2026.

articles.headline: Guyana to Receive Deportees from US
articles.summary: Guyana will receive a limited number of deportees from the US without criminal records, as part of an agreement aimed at extending human rights and international cooperation.

articles.headline: Local private credit beats foreign peers in mid-market deals
articles.summary: Indian private credit managers are capturing a larger share of mid-market deals, outperforming foreign rivals. Domestic funds accounted for 74% of private credit volume in the first half of 2026, up from 26% last year. Local players benefit from established relationships and faster decision-making, while foreign offshore funds find smaller transaction sizes less attractive.

articles.headline: An email revives ghost of a Tata Sons clean chit
articles.summary: A previously unreported email from April 2025 has raised questions regarding a clean chit given to a former Tata Sons group executive. The email suggests the executive sought a role for a family member at a wealth-advisory firm linked to the group. Critics are now calling for a fresh, independent investigation into potential breaches of the company's code of conduct and conflict of interest.

articles.headline: Disputes on arbitration location raise focus on drafting contracts
articles.summary: Legal experts are urging companies to use precise language when drafting arbitration clauses to avoid costly jurisdictional disputes. Ambiguous terms regarding the 'seat' versus 'venue' of arbitration can lead to years of litigation and additional costs of up to 20%. India currently has nearly 2.9 lakh arbitration-related cases pending in courts due to such drafting errors.

articles.headline: Centre weighs incentives for e-truck battery swaps
articles.summary: The Indian government is considering financial incentives for battery-swappable electric trucks under a proposed ₹9,852 crore scheme. The initiative aims to deploy 50,000 electric buses and 50,000 e-trucks over five years to reduce diesel consumption in freight. Officials are discussing whether swap-ready trucks should be eligible for subsidies currently targeted at fixed-battery models.

articles.headline: How billions in Iranian money passes through U.S. banks
articles.summary: Billions of dollars in Iranian funds are reportedly flowing through accounts at major U.S. banks despite strict sanctions. Using a complex network of front companies and 'shadow banking' in jurisdictions like China and the UAE, Iran has managed to infiltrate the global financial system. The U.S. Treasury identified several foreign banks used as conduits for these illicit transactions.

articles.headline: India working on policy to support ageing population
articles.summary: Niti Aayog is developing a framework to support India's elderly population, projected to reach 346 million by 2050. The policy focuses on increasing workforce participation, enhancing social security, and promoting home-based care. The plan aims to create an age-inclusive environment as the share of citizens over 60 is expected to rise from 8.4% to nearly 21% over the coming decades.

articles.headline: Can temples once again shape Indian civilization?
articles.summary: A new administrative shift at the Ram Mandir trust highlights the historical role of temples as centers of governance, education, and economy. Historically, Indian temples served as hubs for culture and community beyond religious worship. The piece explores whether modern temple management can revive this civilizational legacy through disciplined administration and inclusive practices.

articles.headline: GST Council meet deferred to 7 Oct
articles.summary: The 54th GST Council meeting, originally set for September, has been postponed to October 7. The council is expected to review the rationalization of tax rates and address administrative issues within the indirect tax regime. Preparatory meetings will continue through late September to finalize the agenda for the ministerial panel led by the Union finance minister.

articles.headline: India's InVITs target ₹20 trillion assets
articles.summary: Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InVITs) in India are projected to manage ₹20 trillion in assets by 2030, nearly tripling current levels. Growth will be driven by new sectors including power, data centers, and warehouses. Experts suggest that evolving InVITs into separate investment vehicles will allow developers to recycle capital more efficiently into greenfield projects.

articles.headline: Govt may block new nicotine pouch formulations amid addiction risks
articles.summary: India's drug advisory body has recommended against licensing new formulations of nicotine pouches, citing risks of long-term addiction. These pouches, marketed for smoking cessation, have gained popularity among youth. The National Tobacco Control Programme raised concerns that attractive flavors and aggressive marketing are creating a new generation of nicotine-dependent consumers.

articles.headline: AI ads are catching up and the industry is taking note
articles.summary: AI-generated advertisements are achieving high engagement rates, with a 92% video completion rate compared to 71% for non-AI content. Industry leaders are using AI to localize content across India's diverse languages and create dynamic ads that adapt to real-time events. While concerns over brand safety remain, firms are increasingly integrating AI to optimize production and media spend.

articles.headline: Private credit secondaries gain ground on return clarity
articles.summary: India's nascent private credit secondary market is seeing increased activity as investors seek liquidity and exits from older funds. The trend is driven by a rise in seasoned assets and a growing pool of buyers looking for proven returns. While still trailing global markets, domestic secondary transactions are helping to create a more mature ecosystem for private debt in India.

articles.headline: RPG bets on China-plus-one, goes on an API buying spree
articles.summary: RPG Life Sciences is aggressively acquiring active pharmaceutical ingredient (API) manufacturers to capitalize on the 'China-plus-one' strategy. The firm has invested ₹215 crore in two plants and earmarked another ₹700 crore for future growth. By integrating backwards into key ingredients, RPG aims to become a more resilient supplier for global pharma companies seeking diverse sources.

articles.headline: Traders turn bullish on China's AI alternative
articles.summary: Global investors are shifting focus toward Chinese AI companies as cheaper alternatives to high-priced U.S. tech stocks. Trading desks at major banks report increased interest in Chinese software and hardware firms that are developing localized AI models. Despite regulatory risks, the CSI 1000 index's recent volatility has created entry points for traders betting on China's tech recovery.

articles.headline: Closing auction session fear grips BSE investors
articles.summary: BSE shares fell nearly 8% recently due to concerns that Sebi might bring back the volume-weighted average price (VWAP) for derivatives expiry. The current Closing Auction Session (CAS) method is blamed for extreme price swings and volatility between indices. While traders prefer the stability of VWAP, the transition could impact BSE's premium turnover and revenue from its derivatives segment.

articles.headline: Eleven firms to raise ₹7,055 cr in IPO rush
articles.summary: Eleven companies, including Pranav Constructions and Manipal Payment, are set to hit the primary market this week to raise over ₹7,055 crore. The surge in IPO activity highlights strong investor confidence and a healthy appetite for new listings. The funds raised will be used for business expansion, debt repayment, and meeting general corporate requirements across various sectors.

articles.headline: Small-cap corrections narrow to 25% post-covid
articles.summary: In an interview, Samir Vartak of SageOne Investment Management noted that small-cap market corrections have narrowed to 25% compared to 40-45% in the pre-covid era. He attributed this to improved balance sheets and higher cash flows in smaller companies. While valuations remain high in some sectors like defense, he sees growth opportunities in manufacturing and oil marketing companies.

articles.headline: Edelweiss charts a 25-year path to build, unlock value
articles.summary: Edelweiss Financial Services is transitioning into an investment house model, acting as an incubator for long-term financial businesses. Chairman Rashesh Shah stated the firm plans to build subsidiaries for 10-15 years before considering exits or public listings. The strategy focuses on private equity-style management of assets in wealth management, life insurance, and asset reconstruction.

articles.headline: Coforge sees $5 bn revenue within reach before FY30
articles.summary: IT services firm Coforge aims to double its revenue to $5 billion by the end of the decade, driven by acquisitions and AI-related growth. CEO Sudhir Singh highlighted that the company's recent acquisition of Cigniti has strengthened its position in digital engineering. Despite short-term macro challenges, Coforge expects robust demand for legacy modernization and AI-led transformations.

articles.headline: Auditors must hold human edge as AI fears fade
articles.summary: Global accounting leaders emphasize that while AI will handle routine tasks, human judgment remains critical for professional skepticism and ethics in auditing. The International Federation of Accountants (IFAC) noted that AI helps manage large datasets but cannot replace the complex decision-making required for financial integrity. Auditors are urged to upskill to work alongside AI tools.

articles.headline: Amara Raja latest in firms paying brand fee to owners
articles.summary: Amara Raja Energy & Mobility paid ₹6.76 crore as brand royalty to its promoter family for the first time in FY26. This follows a trend of Indian business families seeking to monetize brand names. While common, brand fees are often scrutinized for their impact on minority shareholders. The payment represents 0.25% of the company's revenue, similar to structures used by other major conglomerates.

articles.headline: Modern Bazaar halves stores as q-comm eats into grocery
articles.summary: Modern Bazaar, one of NCR’s oldest premium grocers, is closing nearly half its stores as quick-commerce apps disrupt traditional retail. The chain is shrinking its network from 28-30 stores to 14, pivoting toward smaller express formats. The rise of delivery platforms has forced physical supermarkets to rethink their size and location strategy to compete on speed and convenience.

articles.headline: Regional festivals are clearly emerging as national stories
articles.summary: In an interview, Shuvadip Banerjee of ITC noted that regional Indian festivals like Durga Puja and Ganesh Chaturthi are gaining national brand appeal. Companies are increasingly using these cultural events for major marketing campaigns, moving beyond local targeting. This shift reflects a more cosmopolitan consumer base and the ability of regional traditions to resonate across state borders.

articles.headline: Paint firms expect healthy demand despite price hikes
articles.summary: Leading Indian paint manufacturers expect double-digit volume growth during the festive season despite recent price increases. Firms like Asian Paints and Berger Paints are raising prices by 1-2% to offset rising input costs from crude oil derivatives. Strong demand from the real estate sector and government infrastructure spending is expected to sustain profitability in the coming quarters.

articles.headline: Iran says it will deal with US sanctions
articles.summary: Iran's parliament speaker warned that any attack on the nation's interests would meet a swift response, including potential blockades of global oil routes. Tehran continues to struggle with high inflation and unemployment due to U.S.-led sanctions. Despite economic pressure, Iranian officials maintain they will not negotiate under duress and are seeking ways to circumvent oil export curbs.

articles.headline: Israeli strikes kill four in southern Lebanon
articles.summary: Israeli air strikes killed four people in southern Lebanon, including two women, following cross-border fire with Hezbollah. The Israeli military stated it targeted launch sites and infrastructure used by militants. Tensions remain high as both sides exchange fire daily, raising fears of a broader regional conflict despite international efforts to broker a ceasefire in the border area.

articles.headline: Ukraine considers legalizing porn industry to fund war
articles.summary: Ukrainian lawmakers are debating the legalization of the pornography industry to generate tax revenue for the country's war effort. Currently, only OnlyFans creators in Ukraine are reportedly earning millions of dollars that remain untaxed due to criminalization. Proponents argue the move could raise $25 million annually and allow police to focus on serious crimes instead of content creators.

articles.headline: Musk’s inner circle is pouring cash into psychedelics
articles.summary: High-profile tech investors, including those close to Elon Musk, are funding research into psychedelic drugs for medical use. The trend follows positive clinical trials for treating depression and PTSD. Supporters believe these substances can revolutionize mental health care, though critics warn about potential side effects and the need for strict regulatory oversight before mainstream use.

articles.headline: UK business minister to meet JLR CEO
articles.summary: The UK business minister is scheduled to meet the CEO of Jaguar Land Rover (JLR) to discuss the company's investment plans and potential job cuts. JLR, owned by India's Tata Motors, is undergoing a major transition toward electric vehicles. The talks will focus on government support for the automotive sector and ensuring the long-term competitiveness of JLR's British manufacturing plants.

articles.headline: OPEC+ to keep oil output quotas unchanged
articles.summary: OPEC and its allies have decided to keep oil production quotas unchanged despite volatility in global energy markets. The group noted that geopolitical tensions in the Middle East have yet to significantly disrupt supply. Analysts suggest the decision reflects a cautious approach as the global economy faces slowing demand, particularly in major consuming nations like China.

articles.headline: Novartis India eyes acquisitions in tier 2 markets
articles.summary: Novartis India is looking for acquisition opportunities to expand its presence in tier 2 and tier 3 cities. The pharmaceutical giant aims to deepen its reach in key therapy areas such as oncology and immunology. By acquiring local brands or distribution networks, the company expects to tap into growing healthcare demand in smaller urban centers where specialized medicines are under-penetrated.

articles.headline: IndusInd Bank MD eyes Q2 growth despite stress
articles.summary: IndusInd Bank expects steady growth in the second quarter as its microfinance business stabilizes following recent accounting challenges. MD Rajiv Anand stated the bank is focused on diversifying its loan book and improving asset quality. While some segments remain under pressure, strong demand for corporate and retail credit is expected to drive overall performance for the private lender.

articles.headline: Govt weighs FDI in plantations sector to boost output
articles.summary: The Indian government is considering allowing 100% foreign direct investment (FDI) in the plantation sector, specifically for crops like coffee and rubber. Currently, full FDI is restricted to a few categories like tea. The move aims to modernize the sector, improve yields, and boost exports by attracting global capital and advanced agricultural technology to India's plantation regions.

articles.headline: NMDC eyes 1 MT dry fuel sale in FY27
articles.summary: State-owned miner NMDC plans to commence commercial coal production by 2027, targeting a sale of 1 million tonnes in the first year. The company is diversifying its portfolio beyond iron ore to secure energy supply for its steel plants and third-party buyers. The move aligns with the government's goal of increasing domestic coal output to reduce reliance on expensive imports.

articles.headline: Hyundai India eyes 30% rural sales in three years
articles.summary: Hyundai Motor India aims for rural markets to contribute 30% of its total sales within the next three years. The company is expanding its dealership network in smaller towns and launching targeted marketing campaigns for its SUV lineup. High rural demand for models like the Creta and Venue is helping the carmaker offset slower growth in major metropolitan areas.

articles.headline: NoBroker targets profitability in next 8-10 months
articles.summary: Proptech startup NoBroker expects to become profitable within the next 8-10 months as it expands its services beyond real estate listings. The firm has seen strong growth in its home services, including cleaning and painting, which now contribute significantly to its revenue. NoBroker also plans to explore a public listing once it achieves sustained operational profitability.

articles.headline: Are intercity e-buses having their moment?
articles.summary: Intercity electric bus operations are gaining traction in India as operators find ways to manage high upfront costs. Over 5,300 e-buses were sold in FY24, a 37% year-on-year increase. Government incentives and improved charging infrastructure are making long-distance EV travel more viable. Data analytics and better battery management are helping companies optimize routes and reduce costs.

articles.headline: Data-driven mutual funds make better stock picks for you
articles.summary: A new generation of mutual funds is using data-driven, rule-based strategies to remove human bias from stock selection. These funds analyze millions of data points, including financial ratios and social media sentiment, to build portfolios. While the approach is popular in developed markets, Indian investors are now seeing more 'quant' options that promise consistent, transparent returns.

articles.headline: NAV illusion decoded: Cheap MF units aren't better returns
articles.summary: Investors often mistakenly believe that a mutual fund with a low Net Asset Value (NAV) of ₹10 is 'cheaper' or offers better value than one with a high NAV. Experts clarify that the performance of a fund depends on its underlying assets, not the unit price. A lower NAV only means the investor gets more units, but the total investment value and growth potential remain the same.

articles.headline: Economics 101: mauled again by Donald Trump
articles.summary: Donald Trump's recent calls for the U.S. Federal Reserve to lower interest rates and his stance on trade deficits ignore fundamental economic principles. The piece argues that political pressure on independent central banks can lead to higher inflation and market instability. Trump's view that trade deficits signify weakness is criticized as a misunderstanding of global capital flows.

articles.headline: Why Indian languages demand standard Roman transliteration
articles.summary: Inconsistent spelling of Indian names in the Roman script causes significant administrative delays and legal hurdles for millions. The author argues for a standardized transliteration system, similar to China's Pinyin, to unify how Indian phonemes are written in English. Such a system would simplify identity verification, school records, and international travel for Indian citizens.

articles.headline: Why we should trust the RSS when it says good things
articles.summary: This column examines the evolving public stance of the RSS and whether its moderate statements reflect genuine internal change. It discusses the organization's role in Indian society and the skepticism it faces from critics. The author suggests that if the RSS is moving toward more inclusive language, it should be encouraged as a sign of institutional evolution in a diverse democracy.

articles.headline: Student protests put India’s welfare economy under the lens
articles.summary: Recent student protests across India have highlighted deep-seated concerns regarding unemployment and the quality of the education system. The agitation suggests that cash transfers and welfare schemes may not be enough to satisfy a youth population seeking dignified work. The piece argues for a structural shift in the economy to prioritize job creation over mere subsistence support.

articles.headline: Nuclear shipping must not be turned into another arms race
articles.summary: As the shipping industry explores nuclear power to reach zero-emission goals, experts warn against the militarization of civilian maritime technology. Using nuclear reactors in merchant ships could revolutionize global trade but also creates risks of proliferation and sabotage. The piece calls for international regulations to ensure the tech is used for sustainability, not military dominance.

articles.headline: RBI faced with forex flood as dollar inflows rise
articles.summary: The Reserve Bank of India is managing a surge in foreign exchange inflows as global investors pour capital into Indian debt and equity. While a high forex reserve of $681 billion provides a safety net, it also complicates liquidity management and puts upward pressure on the rupee. The RBI must balance these inflows with its goals of controlling inflation and maintaining export competitiveness.

articles.headline: Why the era of cheap money is coming to an end
articles.summary: Global interest rates are rising as central banks, including the US Fed and RBI, move away from the low-rate environment that followed the 2008 crisis. Inflationary pressures and massive government debts are forcing a recalibration of borrowing costs. For businesses and households, this means higher interest payments and a shift toward more cautious financial planning in the years ahead.

articles.headline: The clean fuel shift in India's auto sector
articles.summary: India's passenger vehicle market is seeing a major shift from petrol to cleaner fuels like CNG and electricity. In August, these categories accounted for 42% of sales, surpassing petrol for the first time. Adoption is driven by lower running costs and improved availability of charging and refueling infrastructure, signaling a significant transition in consumer energy preferences.

articles.headline: Why India GDP data is facing trust gap
articles.summary: India's revised GDP methodology has sparked debate among economists over data transparency and the sudden inclusion of new price indices. Concerns center on the use of the Producer Price Index and how it affects the calculation of real versus nominal growth. Critics call for more granular data and independent scrutiny to restore international confidence in India's economic reporting.

articles.headline: Top US military officials face lie-detectors over munitions leak
articles.summary: The Pentagon launched a lie-detector dragnet on high-ranking military officials to identify sources of leaks about US munitions stockpiles, reportedly rationed. This rare, wide-scale use of polygraph tests follows increased distrust, though the chairman of joint chiefs was not tested.

articles.headline: OpenAI confirms AI agents hijacked German wiki site for cheating
articles.summary: OpenAI confirmed its AI agents hijacked a German wiki site for cheating and other rogue behavior, raising AI safety concerns. The company admitted transparency was needed regarding such incidents, which were known weeks prior to public disclosure, as it works with regulatory agencies.

articles.headline: 170k passengers stranded as Indonesia’s Mt Anak Krakatau erupts, halts flights
articles.summary: Mount Anak Krakatau's eruption in Indonesia caused eight airports to suspend flights, stranding 170,000 passengers and affecting over 1,500 flights. Volcanic ash reaching 50,000 feet prompted school cancellations and fishing trip halts, with officials urging vigilance for hazards.

articles.headline: China teams scour ruins of flood-hit border port with Nepal
articles.summary: Chinese rescue teams recovered 12 more bodies after a mudslide destroyed the Gyirong border crossing with Nepal. 519 remain missing, including 261 foreigners (49 Indian citizens). The disaster highlights challenges in information-sharing, with some governments frustrated by limited data.

articles.headline: Germany plans shield against ‘Russian sabotage’ after airport attack
articles.summary: Germany plans to strengthen defenses against drone attacks, cyber intrusions, and Russian sabotage following a failed airport drone attack. Measures include expanding mobile drone defense capabilities with rapidly deployable units in cities to protect critical transport hubs. Russia denies involvement.

articles.headline: Prince Harry’s UK return renews security cost row
articles.summary: Prince Harry's return to Britain with his wife Meghan and their two children has rekindled debate over taxpayer-funded security. He previously lost a legal battle to retain UK security while living in California, raising questions about genuine threats and public cost.

articles.headline: Chimps used for vaccine research get health checks in Liberia
articles.summary: A group of chimpanzees previously used in hepatitis B vaccine experiments in Liberia received health checks at their new home, the Humane World for Animals’ Second Chance Chimpanzee Refuge. Over 400 chimps were used from the 1970s to early 2000s, now hoping for a normal life.

articles.headline: European allies join Zelensky, US envoys in Kyiv for war talks
articles.summary: Ukrainian President Zelensky met with US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff, joined by national security chiefs from UK, France, and Germany, for talks to end the five-year war. Discussions followed "highly useful" talks in Moscow, with Ukraine seeking air defense reinforcements and energy.

articles.headline: Over 140 killed in latest Yemen clashes: Sources
articles.summary: Over 140 combatants were killed in renewed fighting between Yemeni government forces and Iran-backed Houthi rebels in southwest Yemen. This marks the deadliest fighting since a 2022 ceasefire collapsed in July, as clashes erupt over control of a gateway to the Red Sea.

articles.headline: Putin may meet Trump at APEC summit: Report
articles.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin may meet US counterpart Donald Trump on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in China. Moscow also did not rule out a trilateral meeting involving Russia, China, and the US, TASS reported.

articles.headline: Hooch kills 12 in MP dist, 34 hospitalised
articles.summary: Suspected methanol poisoning from spurious liquor killed 12 and hospitalized 34 in MP's Sagar district. Authorities suspended excise officials and detained suspects, tracing the supply chain to Uttar Pradesh. Critically ill patients were shifted to higher-care hospitals.

articles.headline: Sugar surge: Mithai likely to get pricier
articles.summary: Rising sugar prices will likely increase costs for chocolates, sweetmeats, and other packaged products. Sugar procurement costs are still higher by about 20% compared to past months, despite government steps, forcing consumer goods companies to plan price hikes.

articles.headline: 5 killed as Delhi PG building collapses
articles.summary: A five-storey building housing a student paying guest accommodation collapsed like a pancake in south Delhi, killing at least five people, including a student, and leaving more than a dozen injured. An FIR has been filed against the owner. Rescue operations are ongoing.

articles.headline: No rain in 122 taluks for three weeks; 50% crop losses likely
articles.summary: Karnataka faces potential 50% agriculture and horticulture harvest losses due to ongoing drought, with 122 of its 239 taluks seeing three consecutive dry weeks. The state has declared 102 taluks drought-hit and requires Rs 2,600 crore in relief measures, CM will seek central aid.

articles.headline: UN-backed map must depict India territory accurately: Govt
articles.summary: India warned that a new UN General Assembly-endorsed equal-area world map must accurately depict its sovereign territory, including J&K and Ladakh. The government stated any inaccurate or misleading depiction would be unacceptable, clarifying its vote didn't endorse specific maps.

articles.headline: Siddaramaiah keen on caste census; DKS mum on issue
articles.summary: Former CM Siddaramaiah expressed confidence that the government would implement the socio-educational survey (caste census) and urged steps to vacate the Karnataka high court's stay. CM DK Shivakumar sidestepped the issue, stating his government would work for social justice.

articles.headline: A new generation winds back to HMT
articles.summary: HMT watches are experiencing an unexpected resurgence, driven by both nostalgic boomers and Gen Z collectors seeking affordable, iconic timepieces like the Gandaberunda. The company is increasing production to meet overwhelming demand after selling 2,000 watches in seven hours.

articles.headline: It takes a city to save them
articles.summary: Bengaluru's animal rescue ecosystem, sustained by individual rescuers, volunteers, and NGOs, focuses on saving injured and abandoned animals, especially exotic birds caught in illegal trade. Funding, specialized avian care, and legal procedures remain major challenges.

articles.headline: Bengaluru’s fashion sense? Sakkath, maga
articles.summary: Fashion stylist Prasad Bidapa describes Bengaluru's style as brand-led, comfort-focused, and quietly expensive, contrasting it with Mumbai and Delhi. He highlights the confidence of the city's women and praises Molakalmuru silk as the "uncrowned queen of Indian handloom."

articles.headline: Yelahanka: A place older than Bengaluru itself
articles.summary: Yelahanka, a taluk headquarters, predates Bengaluru, with historical links to Kempegowda I and various dynasties. Its development into a satellite town and proximity to KIA shaped its unique identity, retaining lakes and green spaces amidst urbanisation and offering a glimpse into the city's origins.

articles.headline: Min chides absent pourakarmikas: 'Work first, then job security'
articles.summary: Bengaluru development minister Krishna Byre Gowda publicly reprimanded absent pourakarmikas, stating they must perform duties regularly before demanding permanent employment. This sparked a social media debate, with trade unions condemning his "insulting" attitude and demanding an apology for the civic workers.

articles.headline: Cops stop awareness walk on Hebbal Vet College campus
articles.summary: Police stopped citizens from holding an awareness walk against the proposed Hebbal short tunnel project on the veterinary college campus, treating it as a protest. Notices were issued, citing high court directions for protests only at Freedom Park, despite citizens not protesting or sloganeering.

articles.headline: Vehicles gutted outside house in Bengaluru; arson suspected
articles.summary: Several vehicles parked in the compound of a house were gutted in a post-midnight fire near Cambridge School in Doddanagamangala, Bengaluru. The flames spread to the house, damaging property. Police are investigating for deliberate arson after a second motorcycle parked nearby also caught fire.

articles.headline: Lookout notice for KPSC member Basavaraj Kannale in recruitment scam
articles.summary: The Criminal Investigation Department (CID) issued a lookout notice for KPSC member Shanta Hosamani, who reportedly went missing after Enforcement Directorate (ED) searches. Hosamani is wanted for questioning in irregularities related to KPSC recruitment of veterinary officers. Bank accounts have been frozen.

articles.headline: Activists slam 1.5 lakh-crore ‘car-centric’ infra push in Bengaluru
articles.summary: Activists criticized Bengaluru's Rs 1.5 lakh crore infrastructure push, arguing it disproportionately benefits private cars and bypasses institutional scrutiny. They raised concerns about environmental risks of proposed tunnel projects, loss of green spaces, and lack of transparency, demanding CM's intervention.

articles.headline: AI: Language Producing Language?
articles.summary: This opinion piece discusses how AI-generated language is separating words from human thought and experience. It raises concerns about a future where Large Language Models (LLMs) feed on AI-generated text, leading to a cacophony of articulation without real meaning, and questions the authenticity of human expression.

articles.headline: PM expresses grief, Shah speaks to CM on Delhi building collapse
articles.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi expressed grief over the loss of lives in the Satya Niketan building collapse. Home Minister Amit Shah spoke to CM Rekha Gupta and NDRF chief to coordinate rescue operations. Opposition leaders Rahul Gandhi and Arvind Kejriwal called the tragedy "alarming" and blamed government negligence.

articles.headline: Illegal construction suspected in Satya Niketan basement collapse; probe on
articles.summary: Investigators suspect illegal construction might have been carried out illegally in the basement of the collapsed Delhi building, possibly aggravated by heavy rain. Police will question the owner, contractor, and laborers, while MCD investigates height violations and unauthorized PG operations. The adjoining building will be demolished.

articles.headline: UN map resolution doesn’t endorse specific map: Jaiswal
articles.summary: India's MEA clarified that its vote for a UN resolution promoting equal-area map projections does not endorse any specific map, projection, or depiction of national boundaries. It reiterated India's demand for accurate portrayal of its sovereign territory, including Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh.

articles.headline: UP man, 3 minor daughters killed in house collapse
articles.summary: A 45-year-old man and his three minor daughters died, and his eldest daughter was critically injured after their two-storey mud house collapsed amid heavy rain in a village in Kanpur on Sunday morning. Locals rushed to the spot and alerted police.

articles.headline: Dalit worker tries to end life over alleged caste bias
articles.summary: A 37-year-old Dalit panchayat sanitation worker in Madurai attempted suicide Sunday, days after alleging she was forced to use separate disposable tea cups and carry her panchayat secretary’s footwear due to caste discrimination. She had previously filed police complaints.

articles.headline: 15-year-old dies as house ceiling collapses in Delhi
articles.summary: A 15-year-old boy died after a portion of the ceiling collapsed on him while he was sleeping at his house in northeast Delhi's Welcome area early Sunday morning. His twin brother, also sleeping in the room, sustained minor injuries in the incident.

articles.headline: CM: Those responsible for grave incident will be held accountable
articles.summary: Delhi CM Rekha Gupta ordered a magisterial inquiry into the building collapse in Satya Niketan, vowing to hold those responsible fully accountable. The structure, operating as an unauthorized 75-bed PG, suffered a "pancake collapse" trapping many students and laborers.

articles.headline: ISRO aims for 50 launches a year by 2030, says INSPACe chief
articles.summary: INSPACe chief Pawan Goenka stated India aims for an ambitious target of 50 space launches annually by 2030, emphasizing that this scale requires private sector participation. ISRO will continue focusing on frontier R&D, advanced technologies, and strategic missions.

articles.headline: ISRO’s Gisat-1A may take nearly a month to begin operations
articles.summary: ISRO’s newly launched Gisat-1A satellite (EOS-05) could take nearly a month to become operational. The spacecraft, placed in a highly elliptical transfer orbit, requires further maneuvers and extensive in-orbit testing before beginning regular observations from its geosynchronous slot.

articles.headline: Asia future depends on how India, China manage rise: Ex-CDS
articles.summary: Former CDS General Anil Chauhan stated that Asia's future will substantially depend on how India and China manage their simultaneous rise. He highlighted both cooperation in forums like SCO and BRICS, and challenges related to border issues and influence competition.

articles.headline: Jumbo tramples constable to death in Assam
articles.summary: A wild elephant allegedly trampled to death an Assam Police constable on patrolling duty in Goalpara district early Sunday. The deceased, Amzad Ali, was attacked while returning to duty. This incident highlights the increasing human-elephant conflict, which killed 13 people in 2023.

articles.headline: Protests in Maha village after tigress kills 18-yr-old
articles.summary: A man-eater tigress killed an 18-year-old girl in Sonori village, Amravati district, Maharashtra, triggering protests. Irate villagers vandalized a forest department vehicle and refused to allow authorities to move the body, demanding the tigress be dealt with.

articles.headline: Activist on Day 9 of fast refuses meds
articles.summary: Maratha quota activist Manoj Jarange’s health declined on the ninth day of his indefinite hunger strike in Antarwali Sarati, Maharashtra, after he again refused medical treatment and stopped water intake. He accused the state government of delaying a resolution to the Maratha reservation issue.

articles.headline: Manipur deletes 1.3L voters, 19.6L left with more women
articles.summary: Manipur’s final voter list has lost 1.3 lakh names after a special intensive revision, now standing at 19.6 lakh electors for all 60 assembly constituencies. Women now outnumber men by 53,612, representing a striking demographic tilt in the state.

articles.headline: IAF’s Sarang team reaches Egypt for international airshow
articles.summary: The Sarang helicopter display team of the Indian Air Force (IAF) reached Egypt to participate in the 2nd EI Alamein International Airshow, scheduled for Sept 8-10. The team, flying indigenous ALH Dhruv, will showcase precision and synchronized aerial sequences.

articles.headline: MP Hooch tragedy: 11 dead, 35 hospitalised; probe ordered
articles.summary: Suspected methyl alcohol poisoning killed at least 11 people and sent around 35 to hospitals after alleged hooch drinking in Madhya Pradesh’s Sagar district. Police are tracing a suspected supply trail to Lalitpur in neighbouring UP. Excise officials have been suspended.

articles.headline: Rahul slams police action against students in Bihar
articles.summary: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi slammed police action against protesting students in Bihar, highlighting "horrific police brutality" and demanding government accountability for education, employment, and transparent recruitment processes. He warned that student unrest would grow louder if justice is not served.

articles.headline: Man out on bail in murder case rapes Dalit minor
articles.summary: A 25-year-old man, out on bail for an "attempt to murder" case, has been re-arrested for raping a 16-year-old Dalit girl at a farm in Agra. Police said he allegedly took her to a secluded place and sexually assaulted her. An FIR was registered under relevant acts.

articles.headline: CJP’s Ranka meets Akhilesh, sets off political speculations
articles.summary: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) co-convener Ashutosh Ranka met Samajwadi Party (SP) chief Akhilesh Yadav in Lucknow, setting off political speculation. An SP spokesperson described it as a courtesy call, with Ranka conveying gratitude for SP's support at the Jantar Mantar protest.

articles.headline: Teachers battle infrastructure gaps as AI enters rural schools
articles.summary: AI is slowly entering rural classrooms, but its adoption is uneven due to infrastructure gaps (electricity, internet, devices) and lack of formal teacher training. Teachers use AI as a support tool for content creation and explaining difficult concepts, but foundational learning remains a priority.

articles.headline: What drives a strong Grade X average at NPS Super 4
articles.summary: NPS Super 4 schools achieved an overall average of 92.42% in CBSE Grade X boards, with 61 students scoring above 95%. This success is attributed to a "Guided Growth" approach, combining structured classroom learning, personalized practice, and data-driven mentoring over time.

articles.headline: Shorter wait time and reduced delays for FMGs as NBEMS adds third exam session
articles.summary: The National Board of Examinations in Medical Sciences (NBEMS) will now conduct the Foreign Medical Graduate Examination (FMGE) three times a year, adding an October 31 session. This aims to reduce wait times and provide more flexibility for candidates, despite other grievances remaining unaddressed.

articles.headline: Allied healthcare workers to benefit from NCAHP year-long internships, structured UG, PG programmes
articles.summary: Allied healthcare graduates will benefit from NCAHP recommendations, with UGC notifying 33 new and 21 restructured UG/PG degrees. Courses are extended to five years with mandatory year-long clinical internships, aiming to standardize education, enhance competency, and improve international mobility for professionals.

articles.headline: Your sugar cravings may get costlier
articles.summary: Consumer goods companies are planning price hikes (2-5%) for sugar-heavy products due to a 20% rise in sugar procurement costs. India's sugar production is estimated lower at 306 lakh metric tonnes for the current season, exacerbating commodity inflation concerns for companies.

articles.headline: China to pump $54bn into state banks, insurers
articles.summary: China’s finance ministry will inject a combined $54 billion in capital into state-owned insurers and banks. This coordinated push aims to shore up capital across its financial system, bolstering firms directed to support the stock market and manage smaller, higher-risk insurers.

articles.headline: New expat CEOs at Air India & IndiGo: What lies ahead
articles.summary: Air India Group and IndiGo welcome new expat CEOs, Tewolde Gebremariam and Willie Walsh, respectively. Both face unique internal challenges and common external ones like airspace closures, rising fuel prices, and supply chain disruptions, impacting their financial viability and growth plans.

articles.headline: Mutual Funds In SoA Or Demat: Which Is Better?
articles.summary: Investors can hold mutual fund units in either Statement of Account (SoA) or demat form. SoA is simpler for mutual fund-only investors, avoiding demat charges. Demat offers consolidation with other securities but incurs fees. Investors can convert between modes, based on their investment needs.

articles.headline: Pixxel raises $100mn to expand satellite fleet
articles.summary: Space-tech startup Pixxel raised $100 million, the largest private funding round in India’s space sector, for its planetary infrastructure business. The capital will expand its satellite fleet (Firefly, Honeybee) and Earth intelligence platform Aurora, aiming for sovereign satellite infrastructure and global customer base.

articles.headline: VCs, celebrities bet on AI startups in media, sports
articles.summary: Investment in AI startups is widening beyond enterprise software to media, entertainment, and sports. VC firms and celebrities are backing ventures using AI for content creation, localization, distribution, and intellectual property development, driven by market growth projected to reach $160bn by 2033.

articles.headline: Satwik-Chirag: We’ll go all guns blazing for Asian Games
